name: cdb
tagline: D. J. Bernstein's constant database: immutable on-disk hash tables with two-read lookups and atomic swaps.
description: cdb is a small C library and file format by D. J. Bernstein for constant databases: a key/value file is built once with cdbmake and afterwards only read. A fixed header points into 256 hash tables, so a successful lookup normally needs two disk reads and a miss only one; readers need no locks, and a replacement database is written to a temporary file and renamed into place, so readers never see a half-built file and crashes cannot corrupt it. It was written for qmail, djbdns and ucspi-tcp and has been reimplemented in most languages. After decades at version 0.75, Bernstein published a new release in October 2025 that adds cdb64, lifting the classic 4 GB file limit. It suits read-mostly lookup tables that are rebuilt in batches.

scale.notes: Classic cdb files are limited to 4 GB; cdb64 raises the limit to exabytes. Any change means rebuilding the file.

strengths: Successful lookups usually cost two disk reads, misses one
Lock-free concurrent readers and crash-safe atomic replacement via rename
Machine-independent format with implementations in most languages
Public-domain code small enough to audit in an afternoon
cdb64 (2025) removes the 4 GB size ceiling
weaknesses: No in-place updates: every change rebuilds the whole file
Exact-key lookups only; no range scans or secondary indexes
Classic format is limited to 4 GB
useCases: Mail and DNS server lookup tables
Read-only configuration or routing maps rebuilt in batches
Static key/value datasets shipped with an application
